book.title: Frankenstein · Chapter 7 — The Storm & the Murderer
book.author: Mary Shelley, Frankenstein (1818), Chapter 7

cast.name: Victor
cast.canonical: a thin young man, round head, neat short dark bowl-cut hair, small round glasses, plain shirt
cast.anchor: small round glasses and a plain work apron

cast.name: Clerval
cast.canonical: a cheerful young man who always wears a black top hat

cast.name: the Creature
cast.canonical: a very tall gaunt BALD creature, chalk-white skin, huge black hollow eyes, sharp jagged teeth, ragged shirt
cast.anchor: a tall gaunt bald chalk-white body, black hollow eyes and jagged teeth

cast.name: Alphonse
cast.canonical: an elderly gentleman with a long white beard leaning on a walking cane
cast.anchor: a long white beard and a walking cane

cast.name: Ernest
cast.canonical: a teenage boy wearing a flat cap

cast.name: Elizabeth
cast.canonical: a gentle young woman with two simple braids
cast.anchor: two braids and a plain shawl

panels.scene: Victor at a table reading a letter, his face collapsing from joy into horror, while Clerval watches with concern; a lamp-lit room

teen.narration: BACK IN INGOLSTADT, A LETTER FROM HOME REACHES VICTOR — AND ITS WARM OPENING TURNS TO HORROR.

bubbles.speaker: clerval
bubbles.text: A LETTER FROM HOME, VICTOR!

bubbles.speaker: letter
bubbles.text: William is dead!—... Victor, he is murdered!
even now your eye skims over the page to seek the words which are to convey to you the horrible tidings.

panels.scene: Victor covering his face with his hands in grief, the dropped letter on the table, Clerval reaching a hand toward him

teen.narration: THE NEWS SHATTERS HIM; CLERVAL CAN ONLY GRIEVE ALONGSIDE.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: NO — NOT WILLIAM!

bubbles.speaker: clerval
bubbles.text: I can offer you no consolation, my friend... your disaster is irreparable.
Tears also gushed from the eyes of Clerval, as he read the account of my misfortune.

panels.scene: a dark flashback: a family searching a dusk meadow with torches, finding a small boy lying still on the grass
panels.composition: wide night flashback, small figures, torches

teen.narration: THE LETTER RELATES HOW LITTLE WILLIAM WANDERED OFF AT DUSK AND WAS FOUND AT DAWN.

bubbles.text: the anguish that was visible in my countenance betrayed the secret to Elizabeth.

teen.quote: About five in the morning I discovered my lovely boy, whom the night before I had seen blooming and active in health, stretched on the grass livid and motionless; the print of the murder's finger was on his neck.

panels.scene: a grieving young woman clasping her hands in anguish beside a covered small body, wracked with guilt

teen.narration: A TREASURED MINIATURE WILLIAM WORE IS GONE — AND ELIZABETH BLAMES HERSELF.

bubbles.speaker: elizabeth
bubbles.text: O God! I have murdered my darling child!

bubbles.speaker: elizabeth
bubbles.text: THE PICTURE... IT'S GONE!
This picture is gone, and was doubtless the temptation which urged the murderer to the deed.

panels.scene: Victor riding alone in a small horse cabriolet down a lonely road, head bowed, melancholy
panels.composition: medium, single figure in a carriage

teen.narration: VICTOR RACES HOME, YET DREAD SLOWS HIM AS GENEVA NEARS.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: I could hardly sustain the multitude of feelings that crowded into my mind.
I passed through scenes familiar to my youth, but which I had not seen for nearly six years.

panels.scene: a sweeping view of the blue lake and snow-capped Alps, Victor tiny on the shore gazing up, weeping

teen.narration: THE SIGHT OF HIS HOME MOUNTAINS BREAKS HIM OPEN.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: Dear mountains! my own beautiful lake! how do you welcome your wanderer? Your summits are clear; the sky and lake are blue and placid.
I wept like a child.

panels.scene: a violent night thunderstorm over the lake and Mont Blanc, forked lightning turning the water to a sheet of fire
panels.composition: extreme wide dramatic storm, no figures

teen.narration: LOCKED OUT OF TOWN AT NIGHT, HE GOES TO THE MURDER SPOT AS A HUGE STORM BREAKS.

bubbles.text: the thunder burst with a terrific crash over my head.

teen.quote: vivid flashes of lightning dazzled my eyes, illuminating the lake, making it appear like a vast sheet of fire

panels.scene: Victor standing on a hill in the rain, arms raised to the lightning, crying out to the storm
panels.composition: medium, single figure, dramatic low angle

teen.narration: HE CRIES OUT TO THE STORM AS IF IT WERE HIS BROTHER'S FUNERAL.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: William, dear angel! this is thy funeral, this thy dirge!
This noble war in the sky elevated my spirits

panels.scene: a flash of lightning reveals the tall gaunt bald ghoul creature standing among a clump of trees, staring at the small horrified Victor
panels.composition: wide; creature revealed at distance by lightning, Victor small

teen.narration: THEN, IN A LIGHTNING FLASH — A FIGURE HE KNOWS INSTANTLY.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: THAT SHAPE — !
The figure passed me quickly, and I lost it in the gloom.

teen.quote: A flash of lightning illuminated the object, and discovered its shape plainly to me; its gigantic stature, and the deformity of its aspect more hideous than belongs to humanity, instantly informed me that it was the wretch

panels.scene: Victor leaning against a tree for support, teeth chattering, a terrible certainty on his face

teen.narration: THE TRUTH LANDS LIKE A HAMMER: HIS OWN CREATION KILLED WILLIAM.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: Nothing in human shape could have destroyed the fair child. He was the murderer! I could not doubt it.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: I MADE THIS...
The mere presence of the idea was an irresistible proof of the fact.

panels.scene: the tall gaunt ghoul creature scaling a sheer rocky mountain face by lightning, almost at the summit, superhumanly agile

teen.narration: AND THEN IT IS GONE — UP A SHEER CLIFF NO MAN COULD CLIMB.

bubbles.text: I remained motionless. The thunder ceased; but the rain still continued

teen.quote: another flash discovered him to me hanging among the rocks... He soon reached the summit, and disappeared.

panels.scene: Victor alone in the cold rain, haunted, imagining the monster as a ghostly reflection of himself

teen.narration: THE GUILT IS UNBEARABLE: HE MADE THE THING NOW DESTROYING ALL HE LOVES.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: I considered the being whom I had cast among mankind... nearly in the light of my own vampire, my own spirit let loose from the grave, and forced to destroy all that was dear to me.
No one can conceive the anguish I suffered during the remainder of the night, which I spent, cold and wet, in the open air.

panels.scene: Victor at dawn hesitating at his father's door, deciding to say nothing, a heavy secret on his face
panels.composition: medium, single figure at a doorway

teen.narration: WHO WOULD BELIEVE A TALE OF A MAN-MADE MONSTER? HE CHOOSES SILENCE.

bubbles.text: I well knew that if any other had communicated such a relation to me, I should have looked upon it as the ravings of insanity.

teen.quote: A being whom I myself had formed, and endued with life, had met me at midnight among the precipices of an inaccessible mountain... These reflections determined me, and I resolved to remain silent.

panels.scene: a quiet study wall with a painted portrait of a noble woman above the mantel and a small miniature of a little boy below it
panels.composition: medium still-life of two framed pictures

teen.narration: INSIDE HIS FATHER'S HOUSE, HIS MOTHER'S PORTRAIT AND WILLIAM'S MINIATURE WAIT.

bubbles.text: Six years had elapsed, passed in a dream but for one indelible trace

teen.quote: Below this picture was a miniature of William; and my tears flowed when I looked upon it.

panels.scene: Ernest, a teenage boy in a flat cap, breaking terrible news to Victor in the study

teen.narration: HIS BROTHER ERNEST BRINGS A SECOND BLOW: SOMEONE HAS BEEN ARRESTED.

bubbles.speaker: ernest
bubbles.text: THEY'VE ARRESTED SOMEONE!

bubbles.speaker: ernest
bubbles.text: who would credit that Justine Moritz, who was so amiable, and fond of all the family, could suddenly become so capable of so frightful, so appalling a crime?
her own behaviour has been so confused, as to add to the evidence of facts a weight that, I fear, leaves no hope for doubt.

panels.scene: Victor's elderly bearded father leaning on his cane, grave, as Victor protests urgently

teen.narration: VICTOR KNOWS THE REAL KILLER — BUT CANNOT SAY. HE CAN ONLY PROTEST.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: Justine is innocent

bubbles.speaker: alphonse
bubbles.text: If she is, God forbid that she should suffer as guilty. She is to be tried today, and I hope, I sincerely hope, that she will be acquitted.
I was firmly convinced in my own mind that Justine, and indeed every human being, was guiltless of this murder.

panels.scene: Elizabeth, tearful but hopeful, taking Victor's hands, pleading for the accused girl

teen.narration: ELIZABETH CLINGS TO HOPE — AND ASKS THE QUESTION THAT HAUNTS THE WHOLE STORY.

bubbles.speaker: elizabeth
bubbles.text: who is safe, if she be convicted of crime? I rely on her innocence as certainly as I do upon my own.

bubbles.speaker: elizabeth
bubbles.text: SAVE HER, VICTOR.
Time had altered her since I last beheld her; it had endowed her with loveliness surpassing the beauty of her childish years.
